## Summary

There is a high severity authentication vulnerability in Traefik's handling of connection-bound backend authentication (NTLM and SPNEGO/Kerberos "Negotiate"). For each new frontend connection, Traefik sends the first backend request through a globally shared transport and only switches that connection to an isolated, per-frontend-connection transport *after* it observes an NTLM/Negotiate challenge in the backend's response. When a client preauthenticates — sending a valid `Authorization: Negotiate` token on its first request instead of following the standard challenge-first (`401`) handshake — the backend authenticates the shared-pool connection on that first request and returns a successful response. Because isolation is decided only after the response is seen, the now victim-authenticated backend socket remains in the shared pool, and it is neither drained nor closed. An unrelated, unauthenticated client on a completely separate frontend connection can then be assigned that socket and act with the victim's identity, performing victim-authorized reads or writes.

Exploitation requires Traefik to proxy a connection-bound NTLM/Negotiate backend with connection reuse enabled, and a legitimate client that preauthenticates rather than following the standard challenge-first handshake. The ordinary challenge-first flow is not affected: it installs a dedicated backend transport before the credential-bearing request, so the authenticated socket never enters the shared pool. This is a distinct issue from GHSA-qqjf-53cj-pwvv (which fixed a missing HTTP/3 transport holder): it occurs on ordinary HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 frontend connections because the credential-bearing first request reaches the shared pool before any holder can isolate it. The behavior was introduced together with connection-bound NTLM/Kerberos support in v2.11.0 and v3.0.0. Traefik v3.0 through v3.6 are end-of-life and are also affected; they will not receive a fix on their own line, and users on those versions must upgrade to v3.7.14.
